intro: You are at Mamure Castle, at Anamur in Mersin province, built over the 12th–15th century. It sits right on the shore. Count its towers if you can — there are thirty-nine — and add its moat, and you have the largest and best preserved castle on the Mediterranean coast.
history: The Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia rebuilt the castle over a Roman fort, and later the Karamanids and the Ottomans enlarged it. With thirty-nine towers, a moat and three separate courtyards, it is the largest castle on the Mediterranean coast. And the sea comes right up to the foot of its walls.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the thirty-nine towers and the moat, then the inner court with its mosque, and the lighthouse tower.
facts: Did you know? The moat still fills with water, and turtles live in it. It is one of the few castle moats in Anatolia that still does what it was dug to do. With thirty-nine towers and its moat, Mamure is the largest and best preserved castle on the Mediterranean coast.
outro: This brings our tour of Mamure Castle to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls have stood against the sea for centuries; let them keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
